name: Chelsea Finn
title: Assistant Professor of Computer Science and of Electrical Engineering
lab_name: IRIS (Intelligence through Robotic Interaction at Scale)
current_direction: Vision-language-action (VLA) models for generalist robot control
Robot policies that self-improve from real-world experience via RL
Scalable evaluation and general-purpose reward models for robot policies
Controllable generative world models for manipulation
RL for LLM reasoning: abstraction discovery and adaptive-length reasoning
current_direction_basis: Inferred from the 2025-2026 publication record retrieved via OpenAlex (author A5005431772, 39 works dated 2025-01-01 or later) and verified individually on arXiv/Crossref. The VLA thread is driven by 'Emergence of Human to Robot Transfer in Vision-Language-Action Models' (Dec 2025), 'pi*_0.6: a VLA That Learns From Experience' (Nov 2025), 'FAST: Efficient Action Tokenization for VLA Models' and 'Fine-Tuning Vision-Language-Action Models' (RSS 2025). The learning-from-experience thread comes from pi*_0.6 explicitly and from 'EXPO: Stable Reinforcement Learning with Expressive Policies' and 'Reinforcement Learning via Implicit Imitation Guidance' (2025). Evaluation/reward modeling comes from 'RoboReward: General-Purpose Vision-Language Reward Models for Robotics' (Jan 2026) and 'PolaRiS: Scalable Real-to-Sim Evaluations for Generalist Robot Policies' (Dec 2025). World models come from 'Ctrl-World: A Controllable Generative World Model for Robot Manipulation' (Oct 2025, revised Mar 2026). The LLM-reasoning thread comes from 'RLAD: Training LLMs to Discover Abstractions for Solving Reasoning Problems' (Oct 2025), 'Just Enough Thinking: Efficient Reasoning with Adaptive Length Penalties' (Jun 2025), and 'Feedback Descent' (Nov 2025). A surgical-robotics line is also active (SRT-H in Science Robotics, Jul 2025; SutureBot, Oct 2025) but was not among the top 5 phrases. NOT based on her biography, which emphasizes older meta-learning work.

evidence.title: Emergence of Human to Robot Transfer in Vision-Language-Action Models

evidence.summary: Scalable real-to-sim evaluation methodology for generalist robot policies. Submitted 18 Dec 2025, revised 30 Dec 2025 (v2). Chelsea Finn confirmed in the arXiv author list.

evidence.summary: Vision-language-action model that improves from its own experience; large multi-author paper led by Physical Intelligence. Submitted 18 Nov 2025, revised 19 Nov 2025 (v2). Chelsea Finn confirmed in the arXiv author list. Her personal page states she is a co-founder of Pi.

evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed journal article on autonomous surgery via language-conditioned imitation learning. Verified via Crossref: issued 2025-07-09, Science Robotics, Finn confirmed in the author list. Shows an active surgical-robotics collaboration alongside the core VLA work.

Stanford Undergraduate or MS Students
If you are a current or admitted Stanford undergraduate or MS student interested in research positions, please read this form.

state_rationale:
'OPENING' NOT UPHELD - CONFIRMED AS OUTREACH BY A SECOND, INDEPENDENT ADVERSARIAL RE-VERIFICATION ON 2026-08-31. Every page below was fetched fresh in this pass; nothing here is carried over on trust.

WHAT IS REAL: an explicitly undergraduate-addressed statement does exist verbatim on the live IRIS contact page (https://irislab.stanford.edu/contact.html, HTTP 200). Under the heading 'Stanford Undergraduate or MS Students' it reads, in full: 'If you are a current or admitted Stanford undergraduate or MS student interested in research positions, please read this form.' That sentence was not fabricated by any earlier pass. It is also genuinely undergraduate-scoped rather than PhD-only: the page carries a separate 'Prospective PhD Students' section, and the instruction not to make contact is confined to that section ('We ask that you do not contact us directly with regard to PhD admissions until after you are admitted'). Her personal page corroborates the channel - https://ai.stanford.edu/~cbfinn/ says 'Prospective students and post-docs, please see this page.' with 'this page' linking to this same contact.html.

WHY IT IS STILL NOT AN OPENING - three independent failures:
(1) THE OPERATIVE ARTIFACT IS UNVERIFIABLE. The only actionable element is the word 'form', linking to https://goo.gl/forms/uJuYOfIBQVPhEEDy1, which 302s to a docs.google.com viewform and returns HTTP 401 behind a Google sign-in wall. I cannot confirm it still accepts responses, and I cannot read any deadline, role, project, or eligibility criterion. The lab's postdoc and visiting-researcher forms return the identical 401, so this is a generic sign-in requirement rather than a deleted form - but an unreadable form cannot substantiate an 'apply now' recommendation either way.
(2) THE LANGUAGE IS NOT PRESENT-TENSE OPEN. It is undated conditional routing language for triaging inbound interest ('if you are... interested, please read this form'), not an announcement that positions are available. Nowhere does the page say the lab is currently recruiting undergraduates, name a term, or give a deadline.
(3) THE PAGE IS STALE AND ITS TIMESTAMP IS MEANINGLESS. HTTP Last-Modified is identical - 'Wed, 24 Sep 2025 21:07:26 GMT' - on index.html, people.html, publications.html AND contact.html, so it is a site-wide static rebuild timestamp and is NOT evidence the recruiting text was reviewed or refreshed. The surrounding site is visibly out of date: the newest item in the News section is dated 5/23/2023.

WHY OUTREACH RATHER THAN WATCH: the lab is unambiguously active and demonstrably undergraduate-friendly, on evidence verified live today. cs224r.stanford.edu returns HTTP 200 showing 'Spring 2026, Class: Wed, Fri 09:30am-11:00am @ NVIDIA Auditorium', 'Prof. Chelsea Finn / Instructor' and a '(c) Chelsea Finn 2026' footer. arxiv.org/abs/2601.00675 confirms 'RoboReward: General-Purpose Vision-Language Reward Models for Robotics', '[Submitted on 2 Jan 2026 (v1), last revised 8 Jan 2026 (this version, v2)]', with Chelsea Finn in the author list. The lab people page names 11 current undergraduates and 17 undergraduate alumni, five of whom went on to Stanford PhD programs.

RECOMMENDED ACTION FOR A STUDENT: a prepared, specific approach through the contact-page form - and only that channel - understanding that no confirmed opening has been verified and that the intake form could not be read. This is not an 'apply now'. No email should be used: see the email note below.
